Real Estate

Homes, renting and property, by the numbers

A home is often both the largest purchase and the largest single asset a household owns, so the decision deserves more than a monthly payment estimate. These guides cover renting versus buying, affordability, how to read housing market data, and how property compares with a diversified stock portfolio.

Closer to retirement, the same questions come back in a different form: whether to keep, downsize or sell, and how a home fits into what you leave to heirs.

Common questions

Should I rent or buy?

Compare the full cost of owning (mortgage interest, property tax, insurance, maintenance, and the return you give up on the down payment) with rent plus investing the difference. How long you expect to stay matters as much as the price.

  • Should I Rent or Buy? The Real Math

How much house can I afford?

The 28/36 guideline limits housing costs and total debt payments as a share of gross income. Treat it as a ceiling, not a target, and leave room for savings and repairs.

  • How Much House Can I Afford? The 28/36 Rule

Is property a better investment than index funds?

Leverage magnifies both gains and losses, and property carries costs and concentration that a broad fund does not. The model lets you change rates, leverage and time to see where the answer flips.

  • Real Estate vs. Stocks

What is the housing market doing?

Headline numbers can point in opposite directions. The articles explain what the data measures and what it leaves out.

  • The Buyer's Market With No Buyers
  • Real Estate Blog Archive

What if I sell my home?

When you sell your main home, IRS rules let you exclude up to $250,000 of gain ($500,000 for most married couples filing jointly) if you meet the ownership and use tests. See IRS Topic No. 701 for the conditions.
